entities.summary: Flash Airlines Flight 604 was a charter flight from Sharm El Sheikh International Airport in Egypt to Charles de Gaulle International Airport in Paris, France, with a stop-over at Cairo International Airport, provided by Egyptian private charter company Flash Airlines. On 3 January 2004, the Boeing 737-300 that was operating the route crashed into the Red Sea shortly after takeoff from Sharm El Sheikh, killing all 135 passengers, most of whom were French tourists, and all thirteen crew members. The findings of the crash investigation were controversial, with accident investigators from the different countries involved unable to agree on the cause of the accident.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The crash of Flash Airlines Flight 604 on January 3, 2004, resulted in the loss of 135 lives, primarily French tourists. The incident highlighted the importance of international aviation safety regulations and led to changes in pilot training and aircraft maintenance standards.
